resources.string: Arc distance along the surface (mm) = radius (mm) × angle (rad). Angle (rad) = angle (degrees) × π / 180. A larger sweep gives a longer arc at the same radius. At a nonzero sweep, a larger radius also gives a longer arc.

At the shoulder, the rounded head of the humerus is the ball, and the shallow glenoid cavity of the scapula is the socket. This synthetic example uses a circular slice of an ideal rounded joint surface. The angle is the size of the sweep from a fixed starting ray, not a direction of shoulder motion. The model does not track real joint motion or estimate contact forces. Its angles are not exercise targets or diagnostic measures.
